name: Bamboo Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Lowlands of eastern myanmar, adjacent thailand, northern laos, and malay peninsula
description: Sickly-green bamboo specialist, found in forests with bamboo stands from lowlands up into the hills. Male has a red crown.

name: Asian Dowitcher
rangeDescription: Siberia and manchuria; winters to southern asia and northern australia
description: Very uncommon large, long-billed shorebird, nearly the size of a godwit, found in coastal mudflats and open marshes. Breeding adult extensively brick-red below, dark and strongly marked with brick-red tones above.

name: Tristram's Bunting
rangeDescription: Siberia to northeastern china; winters to southern china and northern thailand
description: Small and distinctive bunting, usually seen moving around quietly in thick undergrowth. Warm rusty brown with a black-and-white striped head.

name: Rennell Gerygone
rangeDescription: Rennell (southeastern solomon islands)
description: Small warbler-like bird, endemic to Rennell Island, in the southern Solomon Islands. Fairly distinctive within its tiny range; note the slender black bill, gray cap, white throat, olive back, and yellow belly.

name: Orangequit
rangeDescription: Wooded highlands of jamaica
description: A small inhabitant of moist woodlands where it feeds on nectar and fruit. Note the short and slightly down-curved bill.

name: Black-capped Antwren
rangeDescription: Northeastern brazil to eastern bolivia, northwestern paraguay, and far northwestern argentina
description: Small, long-tailed antwren of the middle to upper levels of woodlands and dry forests. Males are gray with a contrasting black cap and eyebrow.

name: Mountain Serpent-Eagle
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern borneo
description: Small, striking eagle with broad, rounded wings. Broad white wing bands and base to tail prominent in flight.

name: Javan Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Mountains of java
description: Typical scops-owl, endemic to Java’s montane and foothill forests. Favors the upper and middle levels of the forest, frequently roosting and foraging in the lower canopy.

name: Chestnut-bellied Cotinga
rangeDescription: Eastern andes of ecuador and far northern peru
description: Rare bird of stunted treeline forest in the high Andes of Ecuador and southern Colombia. Mostly gray with a chestnut belly; male has a black cap.

name: White-bellied Tanager
rangeDescription: Coastal southeastern brazil (southern bahia to rio de janeiro)
description: Endemic to southeastern Brazil. Striking tanager found in the canopy in forest, edges, plantations, and gardens.

name: Tablas Fantail
rangeDescription: Philippines (tablas)
description: A medium-sized, long-tailed bird of lowland forest on Tablas. Dull blue on the head, chest, back, and shoulder with some paler blue streaking on the chest and crown.

name: Light-mantled Albatross
rangeDescription: Circumpolar subantarctic islands; ranges north to 35°s
description: A small, dark albatross with pointed wings and tail. Note the ashy-gray neck and back feathers contrasting with the dark head.

name: Babar Whistler
rangeDescription: Babar (eastern lesser sundas)
description: A chunky, heavy-billed forest songbird endemic to the island of Babar, located in eastern Indonesia between Timor and the Tanimbar Islands. Male is distinctive, with a black hood, a white throat, bright yellow underside, and dull green upperparts with a golden collar.

name: Sierra Leone Prinia
rangeDescription: Montane ravines of eastern sierra leone, southern guinea, and southwestern ivory coast
description: A mostly dark gray long-tailed warbler with a striking whitish eye, buff flanks, and pinkish legs. Local and scarce in a handful of hills and mountains in Upper Guinea, where pairs and small groups skulk low down in very wet forest edge, riverine scrub, and thickets in gullies between 600 and 1600 meters of elevation.

name: Black Heron
rangeDescription: Locally in sub-saharan africa and madagascar
description: Chunky, mid-sized, blackish heron. The bill and legs are black and the feet are yellow.

name: Santa Marta Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: A very distinctive brushfinch endemic to the Santa Marta Mountains of Colombia. It has a simple yet very attractive plumage pattern with a black head, white ear, yellow underparts, and gray back.

name: Hispaniolan Palm-Crow
rangeDescription: Hispaniola
description: Endemic to Hispaniola. A large, all-black, gregarious species of pine woodlands, scrub, and palm savannahs; often found in flocks of up to fifty birds.

name: White-fronted Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Woodland of inland australia, to southern and western coasts
description: Small nomadic honeyeater of the outback, fairly common across arid parts of inland Australia. Mottled gray and brown above, pale with dark streaks below, with bold white forehead, white moustache, black throat and upper chest, and yellow in primary feathers.

name: Pink-breasted Lark
rangeDescription: Savanna of southern ethiopia to kenya, eastern uganda, and northern tanzania
description: An unusual lark with a slim bill and pinkish-brown markings on the face and underparts. Unlike many larks, shows no white in the outer tail or rufous in the wing in flight.

name: Crestless Curassow
rangeDescription: Guyana to southern venezuela, eastern colombia, and adjacent northwestern brazil
description: Large, terrestrial bird of flood-prone lowland rainforest; generally shy and difficult to see. Note all-dark appearance and small, red bill.
